npc_fire_dragon_walk.author: Austin Ginder (directed), Grok Bot in T3 Chat
npc_fire_dragon_walk.prompt:
Create ONE sprite sheet image: an 8-frame walk cycle for the baby fire dragon in the attached picture "dragon-design.png".

THE CHARACTER: Copy the dragon in "dragon-design.png" exactly: the same head, eyes, horns, wing, spikes, spots, colours, tail flame, outline and painting style. Same size in every frame. Side view, facing RIGHT. Only the legs, a small body bob and the tail move between frames. The head, eye, horns, wing and spikes stay identical in all 8 frames.

THE STRIDE: The attached "stride-guide-piggy.png" is Tiny Speck's own walk cycle for a Piggy, cut to 8 frames in the same grid this sheet must use. Use it only as a guide to how the legs move from frame to frame. Do not draw a pig.

THE GRID: 2 columns x 4 rows, 8 equal cells, read left to right, top to bottom (row 1 = frames 1 and 2, row 2 = frames 3 and 4, and so on). Square image, as large as possible (ideally 2048 x 2048, so each cell is 1024 wide and 512 tall).

THE LEGS: The dragon walks with its legs in diagonal pairs:
- Pair A = the NEAR front leg (closest to us) + the FAR back leg.
- Pair B = the FAR front leg + the NEAR back leg.
Draw the far legs (behind the body) a little darker than the near legs, so all four read clearly.
- Frame 1: Pair A reaches fully forward, feet just touching the ground. Pair B is fully back, pushing off on its toes. Body at its lowest.
- Frame 2: Pair A is planted and starting to move under the body. Pair B lifts off the ground.
- Frame 3: Pair A stands straight under the body. Pair B is lifted, swinging forward, its feet at their highest. Body at its highest.
- Frame 4: Pair A angles back behind the body. Pair B reaches forward, about to land.
- Frame 5: the mirror of frame 1. Pair B reaches fully forward, Pair A fully back pushing off. Body at its lowest.
- Frame 6: the mirror of frame 2. Pair B planted, Pair A lifts off.
- Frame 7: the mirror of frame 3. Pair B straight under the body, Pair A lifted and swinging forward. Body at its highest.
- Frame 8: the mirror of frame 4. Pair B angles back, Pair A reaches forward, about to land. Frame 8 leads smoothly back into frame 1.
The body bobs only a little: lowest in frames 1 and 5, highest in 3 and 7. The tail sways gently, opposite to the body bob.

IT WALKS IN PLACE, like on a treadmill:
- The body stays at the same left-right spot in every cell, centred horizontally.
- The feet on the ground touch the same invisible ground line, 85% of the way down each cell, in every frame.
- Nothing crosses into a neighbouring cell.

BACKGROUND AND CLEAN-UP:
- Transparent background if you can; if not, one flat solid magenta (#FF00FF) with no shading, no floor and no shadows.
- No magenta, pink or purple on the dragon.
- No grid lines, borders, frame numbers, labels or text.
inputs: sprite:npc_piggy walk (Tiny Speck, OGA CC0), every third frame as an 8-frame stride guide
made:fire-dragon design, the standing frame of an earlier GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst sheet made from Tiny Speck's CC0 npc_piggy and npc_chicken walk sheets

source.cut: each dragon found by the empty gaps around it, lined up on its snout tip and feet, scaled 0.45 into 360x228 cells (120x76 logical at 3x), 8 across, WebP q92 alpha 100

pld_badge_feast_bringer.author: Austin Ginder (directed), Grok Bot in T3 Chat
uses: the Feast Bringer badge's centre picture (tools/badge-art/badge-specs.json pld_feast_bringer)
pld_badge_feast_bringer.prompt:
Draw the centre picture for a new achievement badge called "Feast Bringer" in the video game Glitch, for a harvest festival called Pot Luck Day. Attachment 1 gives the canvas and size, attachment 2 shows six of Tiny Speck's own badges for the style, attachments 3 and 4 are Tiny Speck's own harvest art to follow.

What it is: a horn of plenty (a cornucopia) lying on its side, the woven wicker horn curling up and back to the left like the one in attachment 3, with a generous harvest spilling out of its open mouth to the right: a whole golden pumpkin pie with a lattice or crimped crust and one slice cut, an ear of yellow corn, a small orange pumpkin, two or three potatoes and a few green leaves. It should feel warm, plentiful and celebratory, the feast you bring to share. Seen from the side and slightly above, like attachment 3.

Colour: warm autumn tones: tan and honey wicker, golden pie crust with an orange filling, yellow corn, orange pumpkin, earthy potatoes, fresh green leaves. Bright and cheerful like the foods in attachment 4, not muddy.

Style: the centre picture of a Tiny Speck "Glitch" (2011-2012) achievement badge, the same family as the six badges in attachment 2: a chunky, friendly, slightly cartoonish object drawn as flat vector game art with soft painted shading, rounded shapes, a clear range from light to dark, a thin slightly darker edge on each shape, and a thick clean white sticker outline around the whole picture (about 14-18 px at this size, like the white edge around the chick and the pumpkins in attachment 2) with a very soft small shadow under the sticker. No thick black outlines, no photo texture, no 3D render look, no gradients that look airbrushed.

Output: one PNG, 800 x 800, the picture alone on a fully transparent background (if transparency is not possible, a flat pure magenta #FF00FF background with nothing else on it). Fit the picture, white sticker edge included, inside the box in attachment 1 (720 x 600, centred, a little low) and keep the top 120 px empty. Draw ONLY the centre picture: no round badge, no coloured disc, no rim, no number, no laurels, no stars, no text, no frame, no watermark. The game adds all of those itself.

The pictures from the original game are a guide to the look only: draw the picture fresh, as its own object.
inputs: sprite:cornucopia_crops and cornucopia_herbs (Tiny Speck glitch-items SWFs, CC0) rendered at 4x as references
sprite:pumpkin_pie, corn, pumpkin, potato icons (Tiny Speck, CC0) as references
Tiny Speck's own badge art (CC0) as a style sheet

harvest_stuffing.author: Austin Ginder (directed), Grok Bot in T3 Chat
harvest_stuffing.prompt:
Draw one item icon for a new food called "Harvest Stuffing" in the video game Glitch, for a harvest festival called Pot Luck Day. Attachment 1 gives the canvas and size, attachment 2 shows six of Tiny Speck's own Glitch food icons for the style, attachment 3 shows the ingredients as Tiny Speck drew them (a bun, a mushroom, an onion and a sprig of herbs).

What it is: a generous helping of golden bread stuffing heaped in a shallow, round, warm-brown baking dish, seen from the side and a little above like the dishes in attachment 2. The stuffing is chunky toasted bread cubes, browned and crisp on top, with little pieces of mushroom and onion and flecks and sprigs of green herbs mixed through, and one small herb sprig on top. It should look homely, warm and tasty, the dish you bring to a shared feast.

Colour: golden and toasty browns for the bread, a warm brown or terracotta dish with a lighter rim, small creamy mushroom and onion pieces, fresh green herbs. Bright and appetising like the foods in attachment 2, not muddy.

Style: a Tiny Speck "Glitch" (2011-2012) item icon, the same family as the six foods in attachment 2: flat vector game art with soft painted shading, rounded chunky shapes, a clear range from light to dark, a thin slightly darker edge on each shape, no thick black outlines, no photo texture, no 3D render look.

Output: one PNG, 800 x 800, the dish alone on a fully transparent background (if transparency is not possible, a flat pure magenta #FF00FF background with nothing else on it). Fit it inside the box in attachment 1 (640 x 480, centred), wider than tall. No white sticker edge, no shadow on the ground, no table, no text, no frame, no watermark.

The pictures from the original game are a guide to the look only: draw the dish fresh, as its own object.
